name: Western Visayas
summary_text: On 10 October 2022 the Capiz State University Office of Student Affairs told students perceived as trans women that they would be barred from university premises unless they cut their hair and wore the uniform prescribed for males, delivering the instruction through campus guards with one week to comply and threatening that they could not re-enroll otherwise; the office attributed the order to the university president. A legal-NGO case study documents the students' subsequent advocacy campaign — backed by paralegals of national LGBTQ organisations, who pointed to an existing municipal anti-discrimination ordinance in Roxas City, Capiz, which the office dismissed as inapplicable — and its later milestone: the first openly trans woman graduating as university valedictorian with highest honours. This is a documented episode of institutional gender-expression policing in a provincial (not metropolitan) setting, reversed by advocacy. No killings from the 2024-2025 national series occurred in this region. The campus directive is a resident-facing action rather than a mechanism a visitor encounters; its force as a region signal is that in a conservative provincial setting expression can be policed by institutional authority without an operational local recourse — unlike Central Visayas, this region has no protective ordinance cluster of comparable reach.

sources.title: [ENG] Capturing Equality in Capiz State University, Fighting for Trans Students’ Right to Dream | Alternative Law Groups
sources.claim_summary: Legal-NGO case study (December 2025): the October 2022 Capiz State University exclusion of students perceived as trans women, the advocacy response, and the later valedictorian milestone. (Article body verified from the fetched copy.)
